content: Tokio provides synchronization primitives in the tokio::sync module. The Mutex allows exclusive access to shared state across async tasks without blocking the executor. RwLock permits multiple concurrent readers or a single writer. Semaphore limits concurrent access to a resource by a configurable count. All three are designed for async contexts and will yield to the runtime instead of blocking the OS thread.

The async-std crate provides channel primitives for message passing between tasks. Bounded channels have a fixed capacity and will apply backpressure by suspending the sender when full. Unbounded channels grow without limit, suitable for low-volume signaling. Oneshot channels transfer a single value from sender to receiver and are commonly used for request-response patterns in actor systems.
